spans.s:
भिक्ष् भिक्ष् (probably for बिहक्ष्,
Desid. of rt. भज्), cl. 1. A. (ep. also P.)
भिक्षते, बिभिक्षे, भिक्षिष्यते, अभिक्षिष्ट,
भिक्षितुम्, lit. to wish to share or partake; to beg
for, ask for; to desire, implore (Ved. with acc. and
gen., e. g. भिक्षे सुमतिं तुराणाम्, I implore
your favour against eager foes, Ṛg-veda 1. 171, 1);
to solicit, to beg alms (with abl. of person or with a
double acc.); to obtain; to ask for without obtain-
ing; to be weary or distressed (?); to speak (?):
Caus. भिक्षयति, -यितुम्, to cause to beg, &c.

भिक्षण, अम्, आ, n. f. the act of begging,
asking alms.
भिक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, asking, begging.

भिक्षा, f. the act of begging, asking [cf. मांस-
भ्˚]; anything given as alms or obtained by begging,
(sometimes in comp. with the object asked for, e. g.
पुत्र-भिक्षां देहि, grant the boon of a son,
lit. a son as alms); alms, food given as alms [cf.
दुर्-भिक्ष, सु-भ्˚]; hire, wages (= भृति);
service.
—भिक्षा-करण, अम्, n. the act of ask-
ing alms, begging.
—भिक्षा-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, going
about begging; a beggar, mendicant; (अस्), m., N.
[]
of a son of Bhoja, (also called भिक्षु.)
—भिक्षा-
चरण, अम्, n. or भिक्षा-चर्य, अम्, आ, n. f.
the act of going about begging, begging, mendi-
cancy.
—भिक्षा-चार, अस्, ई, अम्, = भिक्षा-चर.
—भिक्षाटन (˚षा-अट्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, wandering
about begging or asking for alms, begging, men-
dicity, mendicancy; (अस्), m. a mendicant; N. of a
poet; (अम्), n. the act of begging, mendicancy,
going about asking for alms; N. of a work; भिक्-
षाटनं कृ, to wander about as a mendicant.
—भिक्षान्न (˚षा-अन्˚), अम्, n. food obtained
as alms; [cf. भिक्षाहार.]
—भिक्षा-पात्र, अम्,
n. a mendicant's bowl, vessel for collecting alms,
alms-dish.
—भिक्षा-प्रचार, अस्, m. = भिक्षा-
चरण, q. v.
—भिक्षा-भाण्ड, अम्, n. a mendi-
cant's bowl or vessel.
—भिक्षा-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, living
on alms.
—भिक्षा-माणव, अस्, m. a beggar boy,
young beggar (as a term of contempt).
—भिक्षा-
यण (˚षा-अय्˚), अम्, n. the act of plying for alms.
—भिक्षार्थिन् (˚षा-अर्˚), ई, इनी, इ, asking for
alms, a petitioner for charity; begging; a beggar or
mendicant.
—भिक्षार्ह (˚षा-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
worthy of alms.
—भिक्षा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having
or receiving alms, begging.
—भिक्षा-वासस्, अस्, n.
the garment of a mendicant, a beggar's dress.
—भिक्-
षा-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, living or subsisting on alms,
begging.
—भिक्षाशि-त्व (˚षा-आश्˚), अम्, n. the
eating begged food, subsisting on alms; mendi-
cancy; profligacy, roguery.
—भिक्षाशिन् (˚षा-
आश्˚), इ, इनी, इ, eating begged food, living or sub-
sisting on alms; dishonest; [cf. भैक्षाश्य.]
—भिक्षाहार (˚षा-आह्˚), अस्, m. begged food;
[cf. भिक्षान्न.]
—भिक्षोत्कर (˚षा-उत्˚), अस्,
m. scattering alms.
—भिक्षोपजीविन् (˚षा-उप्˚), ई,
इनी, इ, subsisting by alms, one who lives by begging.

भिक्षाक, अस्, ई, m. f. begging, a beggar, men-
dicant.

भिक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, begged, solicited or ob-
tained as alms; [cf. शूद्र-भ्˚.]

भिक्षितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be begged or
asked for.
भिक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, begging, asking for alms.

भिक्षु, उस्, m. a beggar, mendicant, religious
mendicant (especially a Brāhman of the fourth or
mendicant order, i. e. one in the fourth āśrama or
last stage of his life when he abandons his house and
family and subsists entirely on alms; cf. आश्रम,
महा-भ्˚); a Buddhist mendicant; a particular
Buddha; N. of an Āṅgīrasa (author of the hymn
Ṛg-veda

); of a son of Bhoja (= भिक्षा-
चर); N. of a particular species of plant, = श्रा-
वणी, = कोकिलाक्ष; (उ), n., N. of an Upaniṣad.
—भिक्षु-चर्या, f. ‘a beggar's course of life,’
begging.
—भिक्षु-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a work.
—भिक्षु-सङ्घ, अस्, m. a society of Buddhist
mendicants.
—भिक्षु-सङ्घाती, f. beggar's clothes,
old or ragged raiment.
—भिक्षु-सूत्र, अम्, n. a
collection of rules or precepts for mendicants.
—भिक्-
षुसूत्र-भाष्य-वार्त्तिक, अम्, n., N. of a com-
mentary on the preceding.

भिक्षुक, अस्, m. a beggar, mendicant, a Brāh-
man of the mendicant order [cf. भिक्षु]; (ई), f. a
female mendicant.
—भिक्षुकी-पारक (?), N. of
a building mentioned in Rāja-taraṅgiṇī

भिक्षुणी, f. a Buddhist female mendicant or
nun, (probably a Pāli form.)

भिक्ष्य (fr. भिक्षा), Nom. P. भिक्ष्यति,
&c., to beg or ask for alms, (a doubtful form.)
